title: Validation Lab — Catalyst Kickoff & Success Rubric
content:
Overview:
This doc is the kickoff brief for the Validation Lab for Catalyst (internal customer: HarborTech). The goal is to run a two-week, low-friction POC that proves the end-to-end inference flow (data ingestion -> model selection -> routing -> steady-state serving) and generates measurable cost/latency/quality baselines we can iterate on. This is intentionally scoped to show production feasibility rather than a full feature build.

Primary objectives:
- Demonstrate stable inference for a representative HarborTech workload at 100 QPS equivalent for 5-minute sustained windows.
- Measure token-level cost and p95 latency under two routing policies (low-latency and cost-optimized).
- Run a small quality regression suite (50 golden prompts, 5 key intents) and benchmark against HarborTech's current vendor.
- Validate the private deployment networking and KMS integration necessary for their compliance controls.

Success criteria (hard/pass/fail):
- Functional: End-to-end pipeline completes without manual intervention for three consecutive runs (each run = 1 hour of live traffic replay).
- Performance: p95 latency <= 180ms for low-latency policy; mean token cost reduction >= 20% for cost-optimized policy compared to HarborTech baseline.
- Reliability: No single-service outage > 2 minutes during POC; error rate < 1% for inference endpoints.
- Quality: For the 50-item regression set, automatic metrics: pass if F1 >= 0.88 on intent classification and average semantic-similarity >= 0.92 against gold responses. Observability: all traces and token-level cost breakdowns available in Console.
- Security/Compliance: KMS key rotation proof-of-concept completed and audit logs present for all model invocations.

Stakeholders & roles:
- HarborTech product lead: Dana Whitfield (external) — acceptance sign-off on quality metrics.
- Redwood SE lead: Priya Natarajan — POC owner, runbook owner.
- SE engineer: Omar Castillo — integration lead (data + auth).
- Runtime engineer: Marcus Li — serving/runtime tuning and kernel selection.
- Customer success: Lena Park — onboarding, SLA/contract liaison.
- Security reviewer: Samira Khan — private deployment checklist and audit review.

Workshop agenda (kickoff, Day 0, 90 minutes):
- 0:00–0:10 Introduction & goals (Priya)
- 0:10–0:25 HarborTech workload walkthrough (Dana) — data formats, expected peak patterns, golden prompts
- 0:25–0:40 Topology & integration plan (Omar + Marcus) — network ports, model variants, routing policies
- 0:40–0:55 Observability & acceptance metrics (Lena) — dashboards, traces, cost breakdown
- 0:55–1:10 Compliance and KMS flow (Samira)
- 1:10–1:20 Risks, open questions, decision log
- 1:20–1:30 Next steps, fixtures, and owner assignments

Data & integration checklist (minimum viable items):
- Sample dataset (CSV/JSON) representing inbound prompts, size ~10k rows — Owner: HarborTech
- Auth: OAuth client + service account for replay job — Owner: HarborTech/Omar
- Model package: two candidate models (1. base open model, 1. quantized cost variant) — Owner: Marcus
- Replay harness: replay tool config and pseudo-traffic generator (30m warmup, 60m test windows) — Owner: Priya
- Access to private VPC peering / VPN credentials and KMS key material for test keys — Owner: Samira

Experiment matrix (short):
- Baseline: HarborTech vendor replay (imported metrics) -> compare to Redwood hosted API with low-latency routing
- Variant A: Dedicated routing, batch size tuned for latency, no quantization
- Variant B: Cost-optimized routing, dynamic batching, quantized model variant
Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, quality metrics from golden set, trace samples for tail latency causes.

Risk register (top 6):
- Network isolation prevents KMS handshake -> Mitigation: run KMS in customer ephemeral key mode first.
- Golden set misalignment (customer expectations differ) -> Mitigation: schedule focused annotation session Day 1.
- Model tokenization mismatch causes quality drift -> Mitigation: run tokenization diff tool and include token-level diffs in logs.
- Unexpected capacity throttling in Dedicated pool -> Mitigation: pre-reserve burst nodes and enable fallback to hosted variants.
- Incomplete telemetry -> Mitigation: ship minimal tracing stub and ensure Console shows token-level cost.
- Data privacy concern for replay dataset -> Mitigation: scrub PII in sample dataset prior to import; customer signs off.

Acceptance sign-off template (to be emailed after final run):
- Run windows: dates/times
- Objective checklist: (Functional / Performance / Reliability / Quality / Security) with pass/fail and short notes
- Observability links: Console dashboard URL, trace examples, cost breakdown CSV attachment
- Signatures: HarborTech product lead (Dana Whitfield), Redwood SE lead (Priya Natarajan), Redwood runtime lead (Marcus Li)

Initial timeline (two-week plan):
- Day -3 to 0: access + sample data + initial runbook setup
- Day 1: kickoff workshop, annotation session, tokenization checks
- Day 2–4: integration + minimal serving proof (single-worker)
- Day 5–8: scale tests and routing policy experiments
- Day 9: regression suite run, quality review with customer
- Day 10–11: compliance/KMS verification and audit log export
- Day 12–13: final comparative runs and stabilization
- Day 14: handoff + acceptance sign-off meeting

Decision notes / open questions (notes to self):
- Which exact HarborTech intents are critical (Dana to confirm list by EOD Day 0).
- Decide whether to include KV cache warmup in baseline — impacts latency testing.
- Cost target is soft; need to negotiate delta with customer if baseline numbers are noisy.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- HarborTech: provide scrubbed sample dataset (due Day 0 18:00) — Owner: Dana
- Omar: create VPN peering playbook and test credentials (due Day 1 12:00)
- Marcus: prepare two model variants and quantization notes (due Day 2 09:00)
- Priya: spin up replay harness and baseline dashboards (due Day 1 18:00)
- Samira: provide KMS integration checklist and auditing script (due Day 3 16:00)

Appendix: quick check commands and links
- Replay tool: ./replay --config=harbortech-catalyst.yaml --duration=3600 --rate=100
- Token diff tool: https://tools.redwood.ai/token-diff (internal)
- Console dashboard stub: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/validation-lab-catalyst

Notes: keep this doc light and iterate after Day 1 workshop. Capture any deviations in the decision log and push final acceptance doc to Confluence (link above).
